quests.instruction: Owls are calling from the oak tree, and a bat flickers past the window. The kitchen clock says nine. What is the most likely time of day?
quests.hint: Do the animal clues and the clock agree with each other?
quests.explanation: Owls and bats are most active after dark, and nine at night fits that. Together the clues point to night.
quests.funFact: Many bats eat hundreds of tiny insects in one night.

quests.instruction: Jun packs his lunch, ties his shoes, and hurries for the bus while the Sun is still low. What will he do about an hour later?
quests.hint: Follow his morning forward in time.
quests.explanation: Jun is on his way to school in the early morning, so an hour later he will likely be in class.
quests.funFact: Many school days begin between eight and nine o'clock.

quests.instruction: A child in a northern city wakes at 6 a.m. in January and again at 6 a.m. in July. In which month is it more likely still dark?
quests.hint: Days are shorter in one of these months for many places.
quests.explanation: In many places winter days are short, so the Sun rises later and 6 a.m. can still be dark in January.
quests.funFact: In some far-north places, a July morning at 6 a.m. is brighter than a January noon.

quests.instruction: Nadia sees a crescent Moon, long shadows, and children heading home from school. What time of day is it?
quests.hint: The Moon can be seen in the daytime sky.
quests.explanation: Long shadows and children heading home point to late afternoon, even though a pale crescent Moon is visible.
quests.funFact: A thin crescent Moon can often be seen in the afternoon sky.

quests.instruction: After the school bell rings, a girl plays tag, has a snack, and starts her homework while the Sun sinks. What happens next in her day?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what usually follows homework.
quests.explanation: Homework and a sinking Sun happen in the late afternoon, and dinner comes soon after that.
quests.funFact: In many places dinner time is between six and eight in the evening.

quests.instruction: A garden's night-blooming flowers open, and moths visit them. What does this tell us about when moths are active?
options: All of them only fly at noon
quests.hint: Look at who visits whom.
quests.explanation: Some flowers open at night to attract moths, which are often active after dark.
quests.funFact: The moonflower opens in the evening and closes the next morning.

quests.instruction: Dad switches on the headlights, but the sky still has a pale blue glow. Which time is more likely?
quests.hint: Headlights are on, but it is not completely dark.
quests.explanation: Dusk has a fading glow in the sky, and drivers turn on headlights then.
quests.funFact: Headlights also help other drivers see your car.

quests.instruction: It is the shortest day of the year in Oslo. Which is likely true?
quests.correctAnswer: The Sun sets early in the afternoon
options: The Sun does not rise at all
The Sun sets early in the afternoon
quests.hint: It is a short day, not no day.
quests.explanation: In winter in far-north cities the Sun rises late and sets early, giving a very short day.
quests.funFact: In places north of the Arctic Circle, the Sun may not rise at all in midwinter.

quests.instruction: A child wakes in the dark, sees the Moon, and hears a rooster. Which is likely?
options: It is the middle of the afternoon
quests.hint: Roosters often crow near the end of the night.
quests.explanation: Moonlight and a rooster crowing suggest it is just before dawn, close to the end of the night.
quests.funFact: Roosters can also crow in the middle of the day.

quests.instruction: A shadow is at its shortest. About what time is it?
quests.hint: When is the Sun highest?
quests.explanation: Shadows are shortest when the Sun is at its highest, around midday.
quests.funFact: Shadows are longest at sunrise and sunset.

quests.instruction: Which action fits best with a darkening sky?
quests.hint: What do you need less of when the Sun is low?
quests.explanation: As daylight fades, we switch on lamps so we can see. Sunscreen is for strong sunlight.
quests.funFact: People use sunscreen to protect against strong sunlight.

quests.instruction: Hana watches the Sun slip below the horizon, then sees the first star. Which of these happened first?
quests.hint: The sky must darken before stars show.
quests.explanation: Stars become visible after the sky has darkened from the sunset, so the Sun set first.
quests.funFact: Venus can appear before stars at dusk.

quests.instruction: Which statement describes the time just before sunrise?
quests.hint: Decide what the Sun is doing.
quests.explanation: Just before sunrise the sky slowly lightens, because the Sun is close to rising.
quests.funFact: Dawn is the time when the sky starts to lighten before the Sun comes up.

quests.instruction: A farmer feeds the animals while stars are still out. Which time of day is it?
quests.hint: Stars are still out.
quests.explanation: Stars still shining mean it is before sunrise, when many farmers start work.
quests.funFact: Hens usually lay their eggs in the morning or early afternoon.

quests.instruction: Eli faces the Sun, so his shadow falls on the ground behind him. Where does a shadow always fall?
quests.hint: Hold your hand in front of a lamp and watch where the dark patch lands.
quests.explanation: A shadow forms on the side of an object that is away from the light, so it points away from the Sun.
quests.funFact: A shadow takes the shape of whatever blocks the light, which is why your shadow looks like you.

quests.instruction: Maya's shadow is long on the walk to school, short at lunch, and long again on the walk home. What makes her shadow change?
quests.hint: What lights a daytime shadow, and does it stay at the same height all day?
quests.explanation: A shadow gets shorter as the Sun climbs higher and longer as it sinks lower, so Maya's shadow changes through the day.
quests.funFact: A shadow is a dark shape made where your body blocks sunlight.

quests.instruction: Moths gather around a streetlamp, and the sky is dark. What time is it most likely?
quests.hint: Two clues agree.
quests.explanation: Moths gather near lights at night, and a dark sky confirms it.
quests.funFact: Moths belong to the same group of insects as butterflies.

quests.instruction: The school hallway lights go off, the gates close, and the Sun sits low. Which time is it?
quests.hint: School is ending.
quests.explanation: The gates closing and a low Sun suggest school has just ended.
quests.funFact: A low Sun means the day is nearing its end.

quests.instruction: Mom wakes the family for breakfast, and the Sun shines through the window. Dad sees long shadows. Which is likely?
quests.hint: Long shadows can be morning or evening.
quests.explanation: Breakfast is a morning clue, which settles that long shadows come from the morning Sun.
quests.funFact: In the morning the Sun is low too.

quests.instruction: A hungry cat sits by the bowl at dawn. Which is likely?
options: The family is going to sleep
quests.hint: Cats often get hungry early.
quests.explanation: Cats often wake families around dawn for food.
quests.funFact: A cat's whiskers help it feel its way around in dim light.

quests.instruction: Fireflies blink, frogs croak, and the Moon is up. What would you expect to see next?
quests.hint: Consider the order of the evening.
quests.explanation: After dusk, it gets darker until midnight, so we would expect deeper night.
quests.funFact: The darkest time of night is often before dawn.

quests.instruction: A teacher says, "Please finish before the bell. Lunch is next." The Sun is high. Which time is it?
quests.hint: Lunch is next.
quests.explanation: Lunch is next and the Sun is high, so it is late morning.
quests.funFact: Many schools serve lunch around the middle of the school day.

quests.instruction: A mouse sneaks out from its hole while the house is quiet and dark. Which time is it?
quests.hint: Consider when houses are quiet.
quests.explanation: Mice are often active at night when homes are quiet.
quests.funFact: A mouse's whiskers help it feel its way in the dark.

quests.instruction: The sun is warming the pavement, the ice cream truck is playing music, and shadows are short. Which time of day?
quests.hint: Picture shadows.
quests.explanation: Short shadows and a busy ice cream truck suggest early afternoon.
quests.funFact: Hot afternoon sunshine can warm a sidewalk much more than the air around it.

quests.instruction: A boy hears the garbage truck, sees the Sun rising, and sees dew on the grass. Which time?
quests.hint: Three clues agree.
quests.explanation: Rising Sun and dew mean early morning, a time when trucks start their routes.
quests.funFact: Garbage trucks start early in many places so they can finish before the roads get busy.

quests.instruction: Lena walks her dog under an orange sky. The air is cooling. Her mom starts dinner. Which part of the day?
quests.hint: Cooling air and dinner.
quests.explanation: Orange skies, cooling air, and dinner mean evening.
quests.funFact: The air cools after the Sun sets.

quests.instruction: Which clue is a stronger sign of time than a bird's song?
quests.hint: Some clues tell more than others.
quests.explanation: A clock gives exact time. Many birds sing in the morning and sometimes at other times.
quests.funFact: Clock time and the Sun's position do not always match exactly, because clocks follow time zones.

quests.instruction: A flashlight tag game starts as soon as the last light of day fades. Which is likely?
quests.hint: Light fades before the game.
quests.explanation: A flashlight game starts when it is dark, which is after dusk.
quests.funFact: Flashlight tag works best in the dark.

quests.instruction: A sleepy toddler is carried to bed, and the sky outside is deep blue. Which time?
quests.hint: Notice the sky.
quests.explanation: A deep blue sky and a toddler going to bed point to night.
quests.funFact: Toddlers need about eleven to fourteen hours of sleep a day, including naps.

quests.instruction: You see bright stars, a thin crescent Moon, and a lit window. Which clue is least reliable for time?
quests.hint: Lights can be on any time.
quests.explanation: A lit window can be on at any time of day, so it is the weakest clue.
quests.funFact: Lights can be on at any time.
